label: mid-input steps (t=4-6) after an early s (2nd/3rd token)
explanation: Fires only while the original sequence is being read (99% of mass), at absolute steps 3-8, peaking at t=4-6 (93% of mass at t=4-6). It never fires at t<=2 or in the copy phase, and only weakly at the delimiter. Which sequences it fires on depends on whether s showed up early: an s at position 1 or 2 gives about 80% precision at t=4-6, and the largest activations (top examples like "u s s ...", "1 s s ...") have s at positions 1-2, often doubled. Weaker activations, the bulk of the missed activations, follow an early n, u or w, or an s at position 0. Adding those tokens raises recall but costs precision. It is more often active when the current token is a first occurrence (in_first). Its firing rate drops as the number of digits in the sequence grows, and it is near zero for L=3-4. The dev F1 of the simple predicate is about 0.63 and its mass recall about 0.73.
